title: 2000 Paris–Dakar–Cairo Rally
who: Won by Jean-Louis Schlesser / Henri Magne (Schlesser-Renault) and Richard Sainct (BMW)
summary: The 2000 edition of the Dakar Rally, in its African era: 13 stage towns and bivouacs through Senegal, Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, Libya, Egypt. Winners — Cars: Jean-Louis Schlesser / Henri Magne (Schlesser-Renault); Bikes: Richard Sainct (BMW); Trucks: Vladimir Chagin / Semen Yakubov / Sergey Savostin (Kamaz).

sources.label: CBS News: Dakar terror fears spur airlift

approximate: Stage towns and bivouacs from Wikipedia's stage table. The rally ran off-road between them, so the lines are straight from bivouac to bivouac.

stops.name: Dakar
stops.text: The Paris–Dakar–Cairo: for the millennium, the rally ran east across Africa from Dakar to the Pyramids.

stops.name: Niamey
stops.text: Stage 6: 733 km into Niger. Here a reported terrorist threat cancelled the four Niger desert stages.

stops.name: Sabha
stops.text: The rally was suspended for five days and airlifted from Niamey to Sabha in Libya in giant Antonov cargo planes, a first in its history. Racing resumed here.

stops.name: Waw al-Kabir
stops.text: Stage 7: 469 km timed across the Libyan Sahara.

stops.name: Kufra
stops.text: Stages 8 and 9 via the Waha oasis to Kufra, 647 km on the second day.

stops.name: Dakhla
stops.text: Stage 10, the longest at 852 km, into Egypt's Western Desert; stage 11 looped round Dakhla.

stops.name: Cairo
stops.text: The finish by the Pyramids. Jean-Louis Schlesser won the cars again in his buggy, with Henri Magne, and Richard Sainct the bikes for BMW.
